summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including stage 4 chronic kidney disease, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, alcoholic cirrhosis, and type 2 diabetes was admitted for acute kidney injury and hyponatremia despite reported adherence to fluid and salt restrictions. She had been discharged ten days prior after treatment for heart failure and severe hyponatremia, with a creatinine of 3.5 and sodium of 137. This admission was prompted by an outpatient finding of creatinine 6.8 and sodium 128. Initial management focused on evaluation for reversible causes, including autoimmune and infectious etiologies, all of which were negative. Due to persistent kidney dysfunction and fluid overload, a tunneled dialysis catheter was placed on hospital day 4, and intermittent hemodialysis was initiated. She responded well, with improved volume status, rising sodium, and stable vital signs. She was discharged to home with plans for outpatient dialysis and close nephrology follow-up.
problems: Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease with heart failure and stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
Alcoholic cirrhosis of liver without ascites
